name: HTA four-bedroom study house
observed: Two storeys; internal envelope 6.9 × 8.2 m (approximate schedule). LTH 207 has front entrance, central stair, rear kitchen/utility exit.
lesson: A wide-front house still has a room-and-stair plan, not a window grid.
gaps: Unlocated archetype, not independent built survey; roof, setbacks, opening dimensions unknown.
standing: Published design archetype; internal envelope only
views: Ground/first plans LTH 207 inspected; no built photographs or section.

name: 33 Porson Road, existing house
observed: Existing detached house: width 15.9 m, unequal depths 11.4 / 15.2 m; eaves 5.4 m, roof 8.2 m.
lesson: Even a large house can be an assembly of unequal wings. A bounding box is not sealed footprint area.
gaps: No as-built survey supplied; no opening or roof-span dimensions; do not equate proposal to existing house.
standing: Existing dimensions reported in planning assessment; bounding extent
views: Report table; plans listed but not inspected; rear and roof photographs missing.

name: Mill Road Block E
observed: Detached proposal; 9.5 × 9.5 m; eaves 5.5 m and ridge 7.8 m; described as three storeys.
lesson: Storey counts can include roof accommodation; eaves height / storeys is not floor-to-floor height.
gaps: Completion unverified; section, roof form and opening sizes missing.
views: Dimension schedule visually checked; plans/photographs not acquired.

name: 17–23 Constance Street
observed: Two storeys and two bays per house; stone walls, Welsh slate; projecting gabled ends, gutter brackets and a level step.
lesson: Keep the row coherent; let end conditions and terrain account for variations.
gaps: Metric frontage, pitch, plot and access plan missing. Listing is not a measured survey.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: HTA two-bedroom study house
observed: Approximate internal width/depth 3.9 / 8.0 m; two storeys; 62 m² GIA; stated external frontage 4500 mm.
lesson: A narrow plan locates stairs and separate front/rear rooms.
gaps: Not a northern historic sample; external depth and roof dimensions missing.
standing: Published design archetype; internal envelope only
views: Ground/first plans LTH 201 inspected; no photos or roof section.

name: Goldsmith Street
observed: Architect specifies 14 m wide streets. Viewed photo shows repeated entrances, deep opening surrounds, rainwater pipes and asymmetric roof lines.
lesson: Later infill can keep the street rhythm while changing wall/roof construction.
gaps: Street-width endpoints not defined here; not a carriageway width. Individual footprint, heights and pitch unmeasured.
views: Street photo visually inspected; linked project images; rear and measured section unavailable.

name: Shirley Street and 107 Saltaire Road
observed: Two-storey row with shopfronts at ends; No107 is a single-storey rear attachment with rounded corner.
lesson: A corner can be made by an attached shop; it need not inflate the entire house.
gaps: No verified shop/residential internal separation, metric widths or capacity.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: 15–17 Victoria Road
observed: Two-storey houses and shops; nine bays across the composition; central shop entrance and parapet.
lesson: Shop scale and the upper facade composition differ. Parapet is not proof of a flat roof.
gaps: Not independently established as a corner; retained as a mixed-use range control. Footprint, stairs and dwelling counts missing.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: 1 West Parade / West Parade corner condition
period: Historic streets with later alterations; precise date not extracted
observed: Character study identifies rounded corner at No1 and larger corner compositions; documents modern shopfront insertions nearby.
lesson: Turn the frontage around the junction; later shopfront changes belong to specific bays.
gaps: Mixed use at No1 not established; public-house and shop evidence belongs to nearby examples. No metre dimensions.
standing: Local character example; use and metric gaps
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: Mill Road Blocks A–C
observed: C: 24 × 7.8 m, eaves 6.5 m, ridge 8.5 m, six flats; B/B1: 18 × 9.8 m; A: 18.5 × 16 m.
lesson: Width alone does not make a giant house. Keep the dimensional pairs and access questions together.
gaps: Same project, not three independent examples. Roof storeys and stair layouts unverified.
standing: Documented proposal; C drawn, A/B retained in table
views: Dimension schedule visually inspected; not a verified built elevation.

name: Isokon Flats
observed: Reinforced concrete; flat roof; four storeys and penthouse; gallery access and stair tower; listing describes 36 flats.
lesson: Flat roofs belong to an assembly with edges, access and drainage; galleries explain repeated units.
gaps: Not ordinary northern vernacular; deliberate construction contrast. Historical listing count not current occupancy; metre dimensions absent.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: Marmalade Lane apartments
observed: Documented 75 m² apartment type with shared lobby/lift; separate paired-flat types have their own front doors. Timber construction.
lesson: Both shared and individual access exist: choose a plan before placing doors.
gaps: Type D illustration has no scale; unit area does not establish whole-block footprint or occupancy.
views: Unscaled Type D axonometric inspected; project photos linked; measured plans/sections missing.

name: Peabody Estate Blackfriars
observed: Original four-storey blocks: seven-window court fronts, six-window backs with stair recesses; two connected courts, later five-storey additions.
lesson: A courtyard may be formed by separate blocks with gaps, not a continuous hollow rectangle.
gaps: Court dimensions, wing depth and dwelling areas missing; no northern replication justified.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: Lichfield Court
observed: 211 flats over 17 shops across two blocks; courtyard galleries, multiple stairs/lifts; lower ground on falling site; flat roofs.
lesson: Large perimeter forms need an access system and explicit corner/level handling.
gaps: Estate-level counts not per wing; no court or structural span dimensions; scale exceeds the initial small block.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified

name: Marmalade Lane shared garden
observed: Terraces and apartments frame shared garden and car-free lane; 42 homes across whole scheme.
lesson: Adapt family to grouped garden blocks; a continuous ring is not required.
gaps: Same project as A03: not independent evidence. Shared-garden dimensions unavailable.
standing: Built grouped housing; cross-listed, counted once as a project
views: Project garden and lane photographs linked; not a measured site plan.

name: J W Evans, 54–57 Albion Street
observed: Narrow brick/slate rear ranges and later glazed yard roofs; aerial photograph shows several roof assemblies behind domestic fronts.
lesson: Add a workshop range because production and access need it; valleys, chimneys and glazed links follow that history.
gaps: No measured spans, heights or worker area; perspective photo not scaled.
views: Fig4 aerial (front/rear/roof) visually inspected; DP045426 roof photograph linked; section missing.

name: Newman Brothers Coffin Works
period: Listing dates 1892; conservation account says built 1894
observed: Nine-bay, three-storey front; waggon entrance; narrow rear court and workshop ranges; red brick, blue plinth, slate.
lesson: Distinguish loading passage, office stair and workroom access. Parallel roofs alone do not describe a factory.
gaps: Date discrepancy retained; footprint, pitch, openings and structural dimensions missing.
views: Source-linked exterior; rear/roof/section not independently verified
